mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5% in the month preceding the forecast period is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financial conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0 in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-inflation regimes when FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening labor market and supply-side pressure, predicting negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant when both indicators move in opposite directions.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in home sales (HOUST) above 2% of the prior month's level coincides with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals consumer confidence and demand recovery.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 2% from prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive or are negative despite the HOUST surge.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects persistent supply-side contraction.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or equal to mean during steady-state contraction periods.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a positive 60-day forward return as the market anticipates rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3.0 and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when CPIAUCSL stays above 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in job openings (PAYEMS) by over 10% month-over-month triggers a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals labor market strength and optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when PAYEMS increases by ≤10%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in retail sales (HOUST) and consumer spending (PAYEMS) by at least 3% in the same quarter predict a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return through optimism about demand growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and PAYEMS both increase by ≥3% in the same quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive when both proxies rise by <3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it suggests labor market saturation and potential softening in business conditions.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the UNRATE <4.0 three-month window.
